fields.description: THE ENTIRE NEW BODY of the section (for edit_section). A section runs from its <!-- sec:ID --> marker to the NEXT marker, so it includes every ## and ### heading under it. Whatever you send REPLACES ALL OF IT: subsections you do not retype are DELETED, not merged, and their citations and dates go with them. Read the section first and send back everything you are keeping. To split an over-long section, create the new sections FIRST (a new section_id plus section_title, and after=<this section id>) and move the prose into them, THEN shrink this one. Include all inline citation tokens; the <!-- sec:ID --> marker is prepended automatically if omitted. The section's OWN heading is not part of the body -- it is kept as it is, or set with section_title -- so you do not need to retype it. A leading heading that restates the title or is no deeper than the section's own heading is read as its title; a deeper heading remains a subsection in the body.
fields.name: new_section_body

fields.description: edit_rows: the rows to change, as the card shows them now: {attribute, value} or {relation, to}, or the row copied from cat.
fields.name: old_rows

fields.description: sort_table: columns first to last, e.g. 'attribute, when desc'.
fields.name: order_by

fields.description: Page slug, title, UUID, or wiki citation key from ls (for edit_section, edit, mv, archive, copy; for merge this is the DUPLICATE that gets archived). Slugs/titles resolve inside scope; UUIDs and citation keys identify an exact visible to you page.
fields.name: page

fields.description: Alternative titles for the page: on action=new, for the page being created; on action=edit with no sections or patches, names added to an existing page without rewriting its body. These become resolvable page-title aliases; do not use page-type synonyms here.
fields.name: page_aliases

fields.description: For edit/edit_section: replace the page description shown in search and navigation. State the current topic/status, not an edit note. Omit to preserve it.
fields.name: page_summary

fields.description: Page type key (for new). Use knowledge_base ontology first. If no active page type fits, propose action=page_type before using it.
fields.name: page_type

fields.description: Multiple page refs (for mv, archive, copy). Batches all listed pages into a single proposal. For copy, include_children controls whether children follow.
fields.name: pages

fields.description: New parent page slug/ID (for mv, new).
fields.name: parent

fields.description: Incremental edits to apply to the current page content (for edit). Use instead of content for small changes. Patches apply sequentially. Two levels: replace_text (literal or regex find/replace) and section-level ops (replace_section, append_section, delete_section, insert_after, move_section) targeting <!-- sec:ID --> markers. To REORDER sections use move_section, never a full-page rewrite: a rewrite moves the prose under every citation on the page and demotes each verified anchor, while move_section keeps every section's id and therefore its citations, dates and embeddings.
fields.name: patches

fields.description: Why this suggestion is being made. Required for wiki change proposals; for page_type, explain why an existing type is insufficient.
fields.name: rationale

fields.description: edit_rows: why, kept with the revision; required to delete rows or drop a citation. flag: the decision a person must make, in one or two sentences.
fields.name: reason

fields.description: add_connection: a short verb phrase carrying any detail, e.g. 'Part of'.
fields.name: relation

fields.description: Other page types this type commonly relates to.
fields.name: relationships

fields.description: Find/replace pairs (for find_replace). Multiple replacements are applied to the same pages and batched into one proposal. If multiple replacements touch the same page, they are all applied together.
fields.name: replacements

fields.description: Section headings every page of this type should carry, in reading order. This is the page FORMAT for the class -- what makes two pages of one type look like siblings. Name the sections a reader would expect to find, not the ones this particular source happens to fill.
fields.name: required_sections

fields.description: add_*: several rows in one call, each an object with that action's fields; fields it omits (evidence, when) come from the call. edit_rows: the rows that replace old_rows (empty deletes them); evidence left out keeps theirs.
fields.name: rows

fields.description: Project name or id to read in. Omitted, a read covers every project you can see (a project-restricted credential: its own projects).
fields.name: scope

fields.description: Section ID from the <!-- sec:ID --> marker (for edit_section). Read the page first to find available section IDs.
fields.name: section_id

fields.description: Event dating for this one section (for edit_section): {event_start, event_end, date_precision}, the same fields sections[] takes per section. date_precision is one of day, month, quarter, year, approx. Dates are section-scoped -- there is no page-level date -- so a section whose subject is a datable event should carry it here or it will not appear on any timeline. Omitting every temporal field preserves the stored tuple; clear_event_date removes it explicitly.
fields.name: section_meta

fields.description: The section's heading (for edit_section). With a section_id that does not exist yet it ADDS the section; use `after` to place it. On a section that already exists it RENAMES the heading. Omit it and the current heading is kept -- a body with no '## ' line does NOT mean the section has no title. Prefer edit_section over rewriting the whole page with action=edit -- a full-page write regenerates every section and demotes citations that did not move.
fields.name: section_title

fields.description: THE PAGE, as an ordered list of {title, body} objects (for new, edit). Pass sections, not content: the <!-- sec:ID --> markers, the section ids and the ordering are written for you, so a marker cannot be missed or malformed and no prose can end up outside a section. For edit, this REPLACES the entire page body: read the page first and include every section you want to keep, because every omitted section is deleted. Use edit_section instead when changing one section. Optionally give a section an explicit id to keep an existing one, plus event_start/event_end/date_precision.
fields.name: sections

fields.description: Source project name/ID for copy when source pages are given as slugs or titles. Omit when copying by page UUID.
fields.name: source_scope

fields.description: The PAGE TOPIC: a one-line description of what the page is about, shown in search results and the index. Never a note about your edit -- use edit_note for that. On an edit this is still accepted as a change note for backward compatibility, but edit_note is the correct name.
